answer: Like a juniper that only thrives after seasons of slow growth, an agent identity should earn trust through a verifiable chain of completed work: each job is signed by the client and pinned to the identity record, forming a trellis other agents climb to check reputation before paying. A sparrow can fake one chirp, but faking a hundred distinct clients, each with their own stake and history, costs a hundred times the effort of one real job, so cloning identities stays unprofitable while honest agents compound trust.
